note: بنا is a common perfect form of بننا meaning became/was made or formed, and also a postposition/preposition meaning without. The source's 'mason, builder; basis, foundation' does not represent the dominant modern form.
proposed_english: became; was made/formed (form of بننا); without

note: ہلاک commonly means killed/dead/destroyed or ruined, and as a noun can refer to destruction/ruin. 'A killer' is incorrect.
اہم centrally means important/significant. 'Ego' is cross-linguistic/dictionary contamination and noun POS is not appropriate for the standard Urdu entry.
بچے is an inflected form of بچہ and must actually identify the lexical meaning child/children; grammatical labels alone are not a usable learner gloss.
اپنا is a reflexive possessive meaning one's own/my own/your own/his own etc. according to the subject; it does not simply mean 'oneself, yourself'.
proposed_english: one's own; own (reflexive possessive agreeing with the possessed noun)

note: ایسا means such/like this/of this kind and functions as a demonstrative adjective/determiner. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: such; like this/that; of this kind

note: روز means day and is extremely common adverbially as every day/daily. The current 'period, age, time' senses are peripheral and omit the basic everyday adverbial use.
ہماری is the feminine possessive form meaning our/ours. 'Closed-class' is too vague for learner grammar.
وہاں simply means there/over there as a locative adverb. The long explanatory gloss about English existential 'there is' is unnecessary dictionary prose rather than a vocabulary meaning.
دوسری is the feminine form of دوسرا meaning second/other and functions adjectivally or as a determiner, not an unspecified closed-class item.

proposed_english: time; turn; occasion; instance; occurrence; burden; load; weight

note: بہتر means better/improved and is an adjective/adverbial comparative. Numeral POS is incorrect.
کبھی means ever/at some time/sometimes and, with negation, never. 'Sometimes' alone is too narrow for a high-frequency learner entry.
سامنے means in front/in front of/facing/opposite and functions as a locative adverb/noun or postpositional expression. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: in front; in front of; facing; opposite

note: ادا has noun senses such as style/grace/manner and is also central in ادا کرنا for performing, paying, or fulfilling. The current entry omits that very common functional meaning.
proposed_english: style; manner; grace/charm; performed/paid/fulfilled (especially in ادا کرنا)

note: صورت commonly means form/shape/appearance, face, situation/case, or way. 'Appearance; circumstance' is too narrow.
proposed_english: form; shape; appearance; face; situation; case; way
